package.json has no "serve" script (only start, build, test, lint). The README's "Running locally" section should say `npm run start` (after `npm run build`) instead of `npm run serve`.

label: bug
file: none

The reporter describes a real functional problem: after a failed export, the Export button remains disabled until a full page reload, which should not be required. This is a bug in the export UI's error-handling/state-reset logic. However, the searches for relevant identifiers and the expected component files (src/components/ExportButton.js, src/components/ExportButton.jsx) did not turn up any matches in the repository, so I could not pinpoint the exact source file responsible for the issue.

label: bug
file: src/components/ExportButton.tsx

In `handleClick`, `exportReport(...).then(...)` only handles the success case and resets `busy` to `false`. When the fetch rejects (e.g. a non-2xx response, which throws in `exportReport`), there's no `.catch()`, so `setBusy(false)` is never called and the button stays disabled/greyed out until the page is reloaded. The fix is to add a `.catch()` (or try/catch with async/await) that resets `busy` and shows an error toast on failure.

file: README.md

The README's "Running locally" section references `npm run serve`, but package.json defines no such script (only start, build, test, lint). The closest equivalent is `npm run start` (runs `node dist/index.js`). The README should be updated to reference an existing script instead of `serve`.

label: bug
file: src/components/ExportButton.tsx

In handleClick, exportReport(reportId, format).then(...) only has a success handler — there's no .catch() or try/catch. When exportReport rejects (e.g. because the fetch response isn't ok, throwing `export failed with status ${res.status}`), setBusy(false) is never called, so `busy` stays true and the button/select remain disabled forever, matching the reported greyed-out behavior until a full page reload resets state.

The "Running locally" section references `npm run serve`, but no such script is defined in package.json's "scripts" section. The README should be updated to reference the correct existing script name (or the script should be added), so new contributors aren't blocked.
